intake.title: New playbook with questions
intake.intro: Answer what you know about this client; every question is optional. The model writes a draft and shows where each rule comes from.

questions.q1: Who do you represent, and who is the usual counterparty?
questions.q2: The client's industry and size, and the regulation of its sector (financial, health, personal data, government…).
questions.q3: Type of document: lease, services, NDA, purchase, supply, employment…
questions.q4: Jurisdiction and governing law; whether it accepts arbitration, and where.
questions.q5: Risk appetite: conservative, balanced or flexible.
questions.q6: Red lines: what this client never accepts.
questions.q7: What it can give up in a negotiation.
questions.q8: The client's preferred clauses or wording; you can attach them.
questions.q9: Background: past disputes, the relationship with the counterparty, and what went wrong before.

baseline.file: This version started from an uploaded file. LiTT doesn't know who wrote a file, so that text is undetermined.

authorship.pending: {count, plural, one {# assistant edit is still pending, so its text is} other {# assistant edits are still pending, so their text is}} undetermined until someone accepts or rejects {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}.
authorship.rule: This is an estimate from what LiTT recorded, not an AI detector. A sentence counts as the assistant's only if it appears word for word in an assistant edit that someone accepted, or in text the assistant generated. A sentence someone rewrites counts as written by a person. What LiTT can't place is shown as undetermined.
